(def swap!
  "Atomically swaps the value of atom to be:
  (apply f current-value-of-atom args). Note that f may be called
  multiple times, and thus should be free of side effects.  Returns
  the value that was swapped in."
  (fn
    ([a f]
     (if (instance? Atom a)
       ;; As Clojure's Atom.swap: apply f to the value read, validate, and set
       ;; only if the atom is unchanged; if f changed it, run f again.
       (loop []
         (let [v (.-state a)
               newv (f v)
               validate (.-validator a)]
           (when-not (suss.bootstrap/nil? validate)
             (when-not (validate newv)
               (throw (suss.bootstrap/error "Invalid reference state"))))
           (if (atom-unchanged? (.-state a) v)
             (do (set! (.-state a) newv)
                 (when-not (suss.bootstrap/nil? (.-watches a))
                   (-notify-watches a v newv))
                 newv)
             (recur))))
       (-swap! a f)))
    ([a f x]
     (if (instance? Atom a)
       (swap! a (fn [v] (f v x)))
       (-swap! a f x)))
    ([a f x y]
     (if (instance? Atom a)
       (swap! a (fn [v] (f v x y)))
       (-swap! a f x y)))
    ([a f x y & more]
     (if (instance? Atom a)
       (swap! a (fn [v] (apply f v x y more)))
       (-swap! a f x y more)))))
rationale: Expand the complete pinned defn to def/fn, retaining its documentation, all four arities including the variadic one. Follows Clojure's Atom.swap: f is applied to the value read, the result validated, and set only if the atom is unchanged (atom-unchanged?); if f itself changed the atom, f runs again, as Clojure's compare-and-set loop does even on one thread. Watches are notified with the value read and the new value. The arities with arguments close over them.
